mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which stimulates economic growth and increases S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not higher when FEDFUNDS is low (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate indicates economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive when UNRATE exceeds 8% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Increases in both housing starts and retail sales signal strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are not positive when both proxies increase (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth during an expansion signals strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not positive during expansion (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Growth in non-farm payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not positive with payroll growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in GDP indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not positive with GDP growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate and high unemployment indicate economic stress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negative under these conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts growth during late expansion signals strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not positive with housing starts growth (t-test p > 0.05).
